newsitem.title: USA: Vallejo, Calif. eyes $52 mln park debt refunding.
newsitem.headline: Vallejo, Calif. eyes $52 mln park debt refunding.

text.p: The northern California city of Vallejo is likely to issue $52 million of new debt to refund Marine World Africa USA's outstanding obligations, a top city official said Wednesday.
Under the proposal, City Manager Kenneth Campo said a newly-created joint powers authority would issue debt to refund the park's $52 million of outstanding long-term bonds.
"Refunding would allow us to take advantage of lower rates and provide us with operational flexibility," Campo said.
The refunding could save the city up to $500,000 a year in debt service and could take place within 90 days, he said.
The Vallejo city council has adopted a resolution to take over the Marine World Africa USA theme park and assume its long-term debt.
The city council adopted a resolution creating the Marine World Joint Powers Authority, with council members serving as the authority's board of directors.
Effective Nov 1, the non-profit Marine World Foundation will transfer ownership of Marine World facilities, animals, assets and debts to the joint powers authority.
The city decided to take over the park because of declining revenues and attendance. Attendance has fallen about 19 percent since 1995, when some 1.6 million visited the park.
